claims.statement: For a finite CTMC with common initial law, common transition support, and signal-sensitive rates q_theta(x,y)=theta*a(x,y) while all reset/leakage rates are theta-independent, the fully observed path has log-likelihood ratio K*log(theta1/theta0)-(theta1-theta0)*A and path KL E_theta1[A]*d_Pois(theta1||theta0), hence at most a_max*T*d_Pois(theta1||theta0). Any detector with false-alarm alpha and miss beta requires d_B(1-beta||alpha) no larger than this bound.
assumptions: same initial law under both hypotheses
claims.status: internally_proved_conditional_model_theorem; standard CTMC path-likelihood prior art; no external proof review
claims.novelty_boundary: Specialization and consequence of standard path-space CTMC likelihood/KL and binary data processing; no priority claim. It is not a claim about natural systems.

costs.sensor_states: N+1; ceil(log2(N+1)) bits to encode current state
costs.full_path_record: jump labels and dwell times; in reset example E[J_T] <= (theta1+rho)T; timestamp precision is an explicit additional cost
costs.summary: K integer and A real; exact LRT is scalar but finite precision is not free

claims.falsifier: A counterexample within the stated CTMC interface to the path likelihood identity or to the compensator-derived KL expression would falsify the theorem; biological mismatch does not falsify this model theorem.
claims.next_gate: Derive corresponding bounds for partially observed paths or for signal-dependent reset/leak transitions, charging sampling interval and hidden-state inference.

claims.statement: In the N+1-state chain i->i+1 at rate theta for i<N and i->0 at rate rho for i>0, the stationary full-path KL rate under H1 versus H0 is [1-(theta1/(theta1+rho))^N]*d_Pois(theta1||theta0); it rises with N by geometric increments and never exceeds the always-active Poisson rate divergence.
assumptions: reset rate rho independent of hypothesis
claims.novelty_boundary: Exact stationary specialization of CTMC path-space KL; no priority claim and no empirical interpretation.
claims.falsifier: Algebraic contradiction in the stationary distribution or entropy-rate identity under the stated generator.
claims.next_gate: Compare heterogeneous forward hazards and multiple signal-sensitive channels under a fixed total hazard budget.

claims.statement: If signal s and unknown gain g enter every generator rate only through the product gs, then distinct (g,s) pairs with equal product induce identical full path laws and are not separately identifiable. In the two-state reset chain observed only at stationarity, the endpoint law depends on theta/rho and does not identify a common rate scale.
assumptions: finite CTMC generator depends on (g,s) only via gs for first clause
stationary endpoint-only observation and N=1 for second clause
claims.novelty_boundary: Structural identifiability counterexample from equality of generators; not a biological claim.

costs.path_observation: Even complete path data cannot resolve an exact product confounding without calibration or another rate channel.
costs.endpoint_observation: One stationary state sample has less information than time-resolved transition counts and sojourns.

claims.falsifier: A pair with exactly equal generators but provably different CTMC path laws would contradict the first statement.
claims.next_gate: Characterize identifiable parameter combinations when multiple sensitive channels have distinct known state profiles.
